work.title: Twelfth Night; Or, What You Will
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 2, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. A Room in Olivia's House.

content.text: Enter Sir Toby and Sir Andrew.

lines.text: Approach, Sir Andrew; not to be abed after midnight, is to be up betimes; and diluculo surgere, thou know'st.
lines.plainText: Approach Sir Andrew not to be abed after midnight is to be up betimes and diluculo surgere thou know'st

lines.text: Nay, by my troth, I know not; but I know to be up late is to be up late.
lines.plainText: Nay by my troth I know not but I know to be up late is to be up late

lines.text: A false conclusion; I hate it as an unfilled can. To be up after midnight, and to go to bed then is early: so that to go to bed after midnight is to go to bed betimes. Does not our lives consist of the four elements?
lines.plainText: A false conclusion I hate it as an unfilled can To be up after midnight and to go to bed then is early so that to go to bed after midnight is to go to bed betimes Does not our lives consist of the four elements

lines.text: Faith, so they say, but I think it rather consists of eating and drinking.
lines.plainText: Faith so they say but I think it rather consists of eating and drinking

lines.text: Th'art a scholar; let us therefore eat and drink.
lines.plainText: Th'art a scholar let us therefore eat and drink

lines.text: Marian, I say! a stoup of wine.
lines.plainText: Marian I say a stoup of wine

lines.text: Here comes the fool, i' faith.
lines.plainText: Here comes the fool i' faith

lines.text: How now, my hearts? Did you never see the picture of "we three"?
lines.plainText: How now my hearts Did you never see the picture of we three

lines.text: Welcome, ass. Now let's have a catch.
lines.plainText: Welcome ass Now let's have a catch

lines.text: By my troth, the fool has an excellent breast. I had rather than forty shillings I had such a leg, and so sweet a breath to sing, as the fool has. In sooth, thou wast in very gracious fooling last night when thou spok'st of Pigrogromitus, of the Vapians passing the equinoctial of Queubus; 'twas very good, i' faith. I sent thee sixpence for thy leman. Hadst it?
lines.plainText: By my troth the fool has an excellent breast I had rather than forty shillings I had such a leg and so sweet a breath to sing as the fool has In sooth thou wast in very gracious fooling last night when thou spok'st of Pigrogromitus of the Vapians passing the equinoctial of Queubus 'twas very good i' faith I sent thee sixpence for thy leman Hadst it

lines.text: I did impeticos thy gratillity; for Malvolio's nose is no whipstock. My lady has a white hand, and the Myrmidons are no bottle-ale houses.
lines.plainText: I did impeticos thy gratillity for Malvolio's nose is no whipstock My lady has a white hand and the Myrmidons are no bottleale houses

lines.text: Excellent! Why, this is the best fooling, when all is done. Now, a song.
lines.plainText: Excellent Why this is the best fooling when all is done Now a song

lines.text: Come on, there is sixpence for you. Let's have a song.
lines.plainText: Come on there is sixpence for you Let's have a song

lines.text: There's a testril of me too: if one knight give a—
lines.plainText: There's a testril of me too if one knight give a

lines.text: Would you have a love-song, or a song of good life?
lines.plainText: Would you have a lovesong or a song of good life

lines.text: A love-song, a love-song.
lines.plainText: A lovesong a lovesong

lines.text: Ay, ay. I care not for good life.
lines.plainText: Ay ay I care not for good life

lines.text: Excellent good, i' faith.
lines.plainText: Excellent good i' faith

lines.text: Good, good.
lines.plainText: Good good

lines.text: What is love? 'Tis not hereafter,
lines.plainText: What is love 'Tis not hereafter

lines.text: Present mirth hath present laughter.
lines.plainText: Present mirth hath present laughter

lines.text: What's to come is still unsure.
lines.plainText: What's to come is still unsure

lines.text: In delay there lies no plenty,
lines.plainText: In delay there lies no plenty

lines.text: Then come kiss me, sweet and twenty.
lines.plainText: Then come kiss me sweet and twenty

lines.text: Youth's a stuff will not endure.
lines.plainText: Youth's a stuff will not endure

lines.text: A mellifluous voice, as I am true knight.
lines.plainText: A mellifluous voice as I am true knight

lines.text: A contagious breath.
lines.plainText: A contagious breath

lines.text: Very sweet and contagious, i' faith.
lines.plainText: Very sweet and contagious i' faith

lines.text: To hear by the nose, it is dulcet in contagion. But shall we make the welkin dance indeed? Shall we rouse the night-owl in a catch that will draw three souls out of one weaver? Shall we do that?
lines.plainText: To hear by the nose it is dulcet in contagion But shall we make the welkin dance indeed Shall we rouse the nightowl in a catch that will draw three souls out of one weaver Shall we do that

lines.text: And you love me, let's do't: I am dog at a catch.
lines.plainText: And you love me let's do't I am dog at a catch

lines.text: By'r lady, sir, and some dogs will catch well.
lines.plainText: By'r lady sir and some dogs will catch well

lines.text: Most certain. Let our catch be, "Thou knave."
lines.plainText: Most certain Let our catch be Thou knave

lines.text: "Hold thy peace, thou knave" knight? I shall be constrain'd in't to call thee knave, knight.
lines.plainText: Hold thy peace thou knave knight I shall be constrain'd in't to call thee knave knight

lines.text: 'Tis not the first time I have constrained one to call me knave. Begin, fool; it begins "Hold thy peace."
lines.plainText: 'Tis not the first time I have constrained one to call me knave Begin fool it begins Hold thy peace

lines.text: I shall never begin if I hold my peace.
lines.plainText: I shall never begin if I hold my peace

lines.text: Good, i' faith! Come, begin.
lines.plainText: Good i' faith Come begin

lines.text: What a caterwauling do you keep here! If my lady have not called up her steward Malvolio, and bid him turn you out of doors, never trust me.
lines.plainText: What a caterwauling do you keep here If my lady have not called up her steward Malvolio and bid him turn you out of doors never trust me

lines.text: My lady's a Cataian, we are politicians, Malvolio's a Peg-a-Ramsey, and [Sings.] Three merry men be we. Am not I consanguineous? Am I not of her blood? Tilly-vally! "Lady"! There dwelt a man in Babylon, Lady, Lady.
lines.plainText: My lady's a Cataian we are politicians Malvolio's a PegaRamsey and Sings Three merry men be we Am not I consanguineous Am I not of her blood Tillyvally Lady There dwelt a man in Babylon Lady Lady

lines.text: Beshrew me, the knight's in admirable fooling.
lines.plainText: Beshrew me the knight's in admirable fooling

lines.text: Ay, he does well enough if he be disposed, and so do I too; he does it with a better grace, but I do it more natural.
lines.plainText: Ay he does well enough if he be disposed and so do I too he does it with a better grace but I do it more natural

lines.text: [Sings.] O' the twelfth day of December—
lines.plainText: Sings O' the twelfth day of December

lines.text: For the love o' God, peace!
lines.plainText: For the love o' God peace

lines.text: My masters, are you mad? Or what are you? Have you no wit, manners, nor honesty, but to gabble like tinkers at this time of night? Do ye make an ale-house of my lady's house, that ye squeak out your coziers' catches without any mitigation or remorse of voice? Is there no respect of place, persons, nor time, in you?
lines.plainText: My masters are you mad Or what are you Have you no wit manners nor honesty but to gabble like tinkers at this time of night Do ye make an alehouse of my lady's house that ye squeak out your coziers' catches without any mitigation or remorse of voice Is there no respect of place persons nor time in you

lines.text: We did keep time, sir, in our catches. Sneck up!
lines.plainText: We did keep time sir in our catches Sneck up

lines.text: Sir Toby, I must be round with you. My lady bade me tell you that, though she harbours you as her kinsman she's nothing allied to your disorders. If you can separate yourself and your misdemeanours, you are welcome to the house; if not, and it would please you to take leave of her, she is very willing to bid you farewell.
lines.plainText: Sir Toby I must be round with you My lady bade me tell you that though she harbours you as her kinsman she's nothing allied to your disorders If you can separate yourself and your misdemeanours you are welcome to the house if not and it would please you to take leave of her she is very willing to bid you farewell

lines.text: [Sings.] Farewell, dear heart, since I must needs be gone.
lines.plainText: Sings Farewell dear heart since I must needs be gone

lines.text: Nay, good Sir Toby.
lines.plainText: Nay good Sir Toby

lines.text: [Sings.] His eyes do show his days are almost done.
lines.plainText: Sings His eyes do show his days are almost done

lines.text: Is't even so?
lines.plainText: Is't even so

lines.text: [Sings.] But I will never die.
lines.plainText: Sings But I will never die

lines.text: [Sings.] Sir Toby, there you lie.
lines.plainText: Sings Sir Toby there you lie

lines.text: This is much credit to you.
lines.plainText: This is much credit to you

lines.text: [Sings.] Shall I bid him go?
lines.plainText: Sings Shall I bid him go

lines.text: [Sings.] What and if you do?
lines.plainText: Sings What and if you do

lines.text: [Sings.] Shall I bid him go, and spare not?
lines.plainText: Sings Shall I bid him go and spare not

lines.text: [Sings.] O, no, no, no, no, you dare not.
lines.plainText: Sings O no no no no you dare not

lines.text: Out o' tune? sir, ye lie. Art any more than a steward? Dost thou think, because thou art virtuous, there shall be no more cakes and ale?
lines.plainText: Out o' tune sir ye lie Art any more than a steward Dost thou think because thou art virtuous there shall be no more cakes and ale

lines.text: Yes, by Saint Anne, and ginger shall be hot i' the mouth too.
lines.plainText: Yes by Saint Anne and ginger shall be hot i' the mouth too

lines.text: Th'art i' the right. Go, sir, rub your chain with crumbs. A stoup of wine, Maria!
lines.plainText: Th'art i' the right Go sir rub your chain with crumbs A stoup of wine Maria

lines.text: Mistress Mary, if you prized my lady's favour at anything more than contempt, you would not give means for this uncivil rule; she shall know of it, by this hand.
lines.plainText: Mistress Mary if you prized my lady's favour at anything more than contempt you would not give means for this uncivil rule she shall know of it by this hand

lines.text: Go shake your ears.
lines.plainText: Go shake your ears

lines.text: 'Twere as good a deed as to drink when a man's a-hungry, to challenge him the field, and then to break promise with him and make a fool of him.
lines.plainText: 'Twere as good a deed as to drink when a man's ahungry to challenge him the field and then to break promise with him and make a fool of him

lines.text: Do't, knight. I'll write thee a challenge; or I'll deliver thy indignation to him by word of mouth.
lines.plainText: Do't knight I'll write thee a challenge or I'll deliver thy indignation to him by word of mouth

lines.text: Sweet Sir Toby, be patient for tonight. Since the youth of the Count's was today with my lady, she is much out of quiet. For Monsieur Malvolio, let me alone with him. If I do not gull him into a nayword, and make him a common recreation, do not think I have wit enough to lie straight in my bed. I know I can do it.
lines.plainText: Sweet Sir Toby be patient for tonight Since the youth of the Count's was today with my lady she is much out of quiet For Monsieur Malvolio let me alone with him If I do not gull him into a nayword and make him a common recreation do not think I have wit enough to lie straight in my bed I know I can do it

lines.text: Possess us, possess us, tell us something of him.
lines.plainText: Possess us possess us tell us something of him

lines.text: Marry, sir, sometimes he is a kind of Puritan.
lines.plainText: Marry sir sometimes he is a kind of Puritan

lines.text: O, if I thought that, I'd beat him like a dog.
lines.plainText: O if I thought that I'd beat him like a dog

lines.text: What, for being a Puritan? Thy exquisite reason, dear knight?
lines.plainText: What for being a Puritan Thy exquisite reason dear knight

lines.text: I have no exquisite reason for't, but I have reason good enough.
lines.plainText: I have no exquisite reason for't but I have reason good enough

lines.text: The devil a Puritan that he is, or anything constantly but a time-pleaser, an affectioned ass that cons state without book and utters it by great swarths; the best persuaded of himself, so crammed (as he thinks) with excellencies, that it is his grounds of faith that all that look on him love him. And on that vice in him will my revenge find notable cause to work.
lines.plainText: The devil a Puritan that he is or anything constantly but a timepleaser an affectioned ass that cons state without book and utters it by great swarths the best persuaded of himself so crammed as he thinks with excellencies that it is his grounds of faith that all that look on him love him And on that vice in him will my revenge find notable cause to work

lines.text: What wilt thou do?
lines.plainText: What wilt thou do

lines.text: I will drop in his way some obscure epistles of love, wherein by the colour of his beard, the shape of his leg, the manner of his gait, the expressure of his eye, forehead, and complexion, he shall find himself most feelingly personated. I can write very like my lady your niece; on a forgotten matter we can hardly make distinction of our hands.
lines.plainText: I will drop in his way some obscure epistles of love wherein by the colour of his beard the shape of his leg the manner of his gait the expressure of his eye forehead and complexion he shall find himself most feelingly personated I can write very like my lady your niece on a forgotten matter we can hardly make distinction of our hands

lines.text: Excellent! I smell a device.
lines.plainText: Excellent I smell a device

lines.text: I have't in my nose too.
lines.plainText: I have't in my nose too

lines.text: He shall think, by the letters that thou wilt drop, that they come from my niece, and that she is in love with him.
lines.plainText: He shall think by the letters that thou wilt drop that they come from my niece and that she is in love with him

lines.text: My purpose is indeed a horse of that colour.
lines.plainText: My purpose is indeed a horse of that colour

lines.text: And your horse now would make him an ass.
lines.plainText: And your horse now would make him an ass

lines.text: Ass, I doubt not.
lines.plainText: Ass I doubt not

lines.text: O 'twill be admirable!
lines.plainText: O 'twill be admirable

lines.text: Sport royal, I warrant you. I know my physic will work with him. I will plant you two, and let the fool make a third, where he shall find the letter. Observe his construction of it. For this night, to bed, and dream on the event. Farewell.
lines.plainText: Sport royal I warrant you I know my physic will work with him I will plant you two and let the fool make a third where he shall find the letter Observe his construction of it For this night to bed and dream on the event Farewell

lines.text: Good night, Penthesilea.
lines.plainText: Good night Penthesilea

lines.text: Before me, she's a good wench.
lines.plainText: Before me she's a good wench

lines.text: She's a beagle true bred, and one that adores me. What o' that?
lines.plainText: She's a beagle true bred and one that adores me What o' that

lines.text: I was adored once too.
lines.plainText: I was adored once too

lines.text: Let's to bed, knight. Thou hadst need send for more money.
lines.plainText: Let's to bed knight Thou hadst need send for more money

lines.text: If I cannot recover your niece, I am a foul way out.
lines.plainText: If I cannot recover your niece I am a foul way out

lines.text: Send for money, knight; if thou hast her not i' th' end, call me cut.
lines.plainText: Send for money knight if thou hast her not i' th' end call me cut

lines.text: If I do not, never trust me, take it how you will.
lines.plainText: If I do not never trust me take it how you will

lines.text: Come, come, I'll go burn some sack, 'tis too late to go to bed now. Come, knight, come, knight.
lines.plainText: Come come I'll go burn some sack 'tis too late to go to bed now Come knight come knight
